senses.gloss:
bhūloka
(‘the earth-world’)
------------------------------------------
Bhūmi or the earth is considered as a ‘loka,’ a place for doing कर्म or actions and enjoy their fruits. Hence, it is this earth with all its living beings, that has been designated as ‘bhūloka.’ It is the first of the three lokas, the other two—higher ones—being भुवर्लोक (the mid-region) and स्वर्लोक (the हेअवेन्). Sometimes, the lokas are enumerated as fourteen, in which case भूलोक is described as situated in the middle, with six lokas above it and seven below.
The surface of this भूलोक is in the form of a lotus leaf, consisting of seven dvīpas (continents or islands) arranged in the form of concentric circles round the central land mass called the जम्बूद्वीप. The other dvīpas are: Plakṣa, Śālmala, कुश, Krauñca, Śāka and पुष्कर. All these are surrounded by oceans containing different kinds of liquids like water, milk, curds or cane juice.
Of these dvīpas, the जम्बूद्वीप is considered as more relevant to us since the भारतवर्ष (the Indian land mass) is situated in it.
For details see Bhāgavata (5.16-19).
